subject: polity
note: Original notes along NCERT civics / political science 6–12. Pair with Laxmikanth and the bare Constitution.

chapters.title: Understanding Diversity
chapters.summary: India’s diversity of language, region, religion and livelihood is a political fact, not only a slogan. Unity is negotiated through the Constitution, not sameness.

chapters.title: Diversity and Discrimination
chapters.summary: Discrimination is diversity plus power. Caste, gender, disability and minority status need legal remedies (rights, commissions), not only moral appeals.

chapters.title: What is Government?
chapters.summary: Government makes laws, implements, and settles disputes. Levels: local, state, Union. Democracy means people can change rulers and demand answers.

chapters.title: Key Elements of a Democratic Government
chapters.summary: Participation, accountability, resolution of conflict, equality and justice. Elections are necessary but not sufficient.

chapters.title: Panchayati Raj
chapters.summary: Village democracy: gram sabha, gram panchayat, three tiers after 73rd Amendment. Funds, functions, functionaries decide if PRIs are real.

chapters.title: Rural Administration
chapters.summary: Patwari, tehsildar, police station, land records. Administration is the face of the state in the village.

chapters.title: Urban Administration
chapters.summary: Municipalities, wards, taxes, water and waste. 74th Amendment is the urban twin of panchayats.

chapters.title: Rural Livelihoods
chapters.summary: Farm and non-farm work, landless labour, cooperatives. Livelihoods explain why welfare and MGNREGA exist.

chapters.title: Urban Livelihoods
chapters.summary: Factories, shops, street vendors, gig work. Informal urban work is the majority story.

chapters.title: On Equality
chapters.summary: Equality in the Preamble and Article 14–18. Universal Adult Franchise. Midday meal as equality in practice. Inequality persists; law is a tool.

chapters.title: Role of the Government in Health
chapters.summary: Public vs private health, Kerala-type public investment vs out-of-pocket spend. Health is a governance outcome.

chapters.title: How the State Government Works
chapters.summary: MLAs, Chief Minister, Council of Ministers, Vidhan Sabha. Debates, questions, and the cabinet system at state level.

chapters.title: Growing up as Boys and Girls
chapters.summary: Gender is social. Housework is work. Equality needs law and culture change.

chapters.title: Women Change the World
chapters.summary: Women’s movement, education, laws against violence, political reservation. History of struggle, not a finished file.

chapters.title: Understanding Media
chapters.summary: Media sets agenda, needs money, can be biased. Democracy needs independent information and media literacy.

chapters.title: Markets Around Us
chapters.summary: Weekly haats to malls and chains. Who has power in the market? Link later to competition law.

chapters.title: A Shirt in the Market
chapters.summary: Value chain from cotton farmer to brand. Putting-out, profits at the brand end, vulnerability at the farm end.

chapters.title: Struggles for Equality
chapters.summary: Movements use the Constitution. Tawa Matsya Sangh-type examples: organisation + rights language.

chapters.title: The Indian Constitution
chapters.summary: Why a long written Constitution: colonial past, diversity, rights. Key features: federal, parliamentary, independent judiciary, secular, socialist (42nd). Rule of law.

chapters.title: Understanding Secularism
chapters.summary: Indian secularism: principled distance, not wall of separation only. State can intervene against social evils. Freedom of religion with public order limits.

chapters.title: Why Do We Need a Parliament?
chapters.summary: Lok Sabha, Rajya Sabha, law-making, budget, executive control. People elect; Parliament represents and oversees.

chapters.title: Understanding Laws
chapters.summary: How a bill becomes an Act, unpopular laws, role of people and courts. Law without legitimacy is brittle.

chapters.title: Judiciary
chapters.summary: Independence, structure (SC–HC–district), judicial review, PIL. Access to justice is the weak link.

chapters.title: Understanding Our Criminal Justice System
chapters.summary: Police, public prosecutor, defence, judge. FIR, investigation, fair trial. Article 22 and rights of accused.

chapters.title: Understanding Marginalisation
chapters.summary: Adivasis, minorities, development-displacement. Marginalisation is structural.

chapters.title: Confronting Marginalisation
chapters.summary: Safeguards: Articles 15, 17, 21, 32; SC/ST Prevention of Atrocities Act; Forest Rights Act. Law + movement.

chapters.title: Public Facilities
chapters.summary: Water, health, sanitation as public goods. Who provides, who pays, who is excluded. Chennai water as a case of urban stress.

chapters.title: Law and Social Justice
chapters.summary: Why markets need labour and environment laws. Bhopal as a warning on enforcement. Minimum wages, safety.

chapters.title: What is Democracy? Why Democracy?
chapters.summary: Features: free fair elections, one person one vote, rule of law, rights. Merits and arguments against. Democracy as a form plus a principle.

chapters.title: Constitutional Design
chapters.summary: South Africa comparison, making of Indian Constitution, Preamble values, institutional design. Philosophy in the Preamble.

chapters.title: Electoral Politics
chapters.summary: Why elections, our system (FPTP), Election Commission, challenges (money, muscle, booth). Democratic elections need a referee.

chapters.title: Working of Institutions
chapters.summary: President, PM, Parliament, Supreme Court through a policy case (e.g. OBC decision). Who takes decisions in a parliamentary system.

chapters.title: Democratic Rights
chapters.summary: Life without rights (Guantanamo-type contrast), Fundamental Rights, NHRC, expanding rights (education, information, food as later laws).

chapters.title: Power-sharing
chapters.summary: Belgium and Sri Lanka: why power-sharing prevents conflict. Forms: among organs, among governments, among social groups, among parties/movements.

chapters.title: Federalism
chapters.summary: What federalism is, India as holding-together federation, Union–State–local, linguistic states, 1992 local government, Centre–State bargaining.

chapters.title: Gender, Religion and Caste
chapters.summary: Gender division of labour, women’s political representation, communalism vs secularism, caste in politics — both as social division and as mobilisation.

chapters.title: Political Parties
chapters.summary: Functions, national vs state parties, challenges (dynasty, money, internal democracy), party system. Need for reform.

chapters.title: Outcomes of Democracy
chapters.summary: Accountable government, reduced inequality (incomplete), dignity. Democracy is a process; outcomes vary by citizen quality.

chapters.title: Political Reforms / Challenges to Democracy
chapters.summary: Foundational, challenge of expansion, deepening. Legal plus political reforms; over-criminalisation of politics is itself a problem.

chapters.title: Constitution: Why and How
chapters.summary: Functions of a constitution, Indian making process, sources, mode of promulgation. It is a living document.

chapters.title: Rights in the Indian Constitution
chapters.summary: WRIT jurisdiction, reasonable restrictions, expanding Article 21, relationship with DPSPs and duties.

chapters.title: Election and Representation
chapters.summary: FPTP vs PR, reserved seats, free and fair, Election Commission’s powers, electoral reforms (NOTA, VVPATs in CA).

chapters.title: Executive
chapters.summary: Parliamentary executive, PM as real executive, President’s discretionary edges, permanent civil service, bureaucracy’s role.

chapters.title: Legislature
chapters.summary: Two Houses, how a bill is passed, instruments of control, decline of debate, anti-defection.

chapters.title: Judiciary
chapters.summary: Independence, appointments (collegium debate), judicial review, activism vs overreach, tribunals.

chapters.title: Federalism
chapters.summary: Strong Centre, emergencies, Governor, inter-state council, GST Council as a new federal site, Sarkaria/Punchhi flavour.

chapters.title: Local Governments
chapters.summary: 73rd/74th, 11th–12th Schedules, remaining weaknesses: funds and parallel bodies.

chapters.title: Constitution as a Living Document
chapters.summary: Amendment procedure, basic structure, 42nd/44th, how politics changes the text.

chapters.title: The Philosophy of the Constitution
chapters.summary: Political equality, social justice, national unity, respect for diversity. Limitations and achievements.

books.book: Politics in India since Independence + Contemporary World Politics (selected)

chapters.title: Challenges of Nation-Building
chapters.summary: Partition, integration of states, linguistic reorganisation. Nehru’s project of unity and planned development.

chapters.title: Era of One-party Dominance
chapters.summary: Congress system, opposition, 1952–67 elections. Dominance was electoral, not the absence of democracy.

chapters.title: Politics of Planned Development
chapters.summary: Planning Commission, mixed economy, dams and industry as temples, land reforms mixed record.

chapters.title: India’s External Relations
chapters.summary: NAM, Panchsheel, 1962/1965/1971, nuclear 1974, look-east later CA. Foreign policy as GS-II.

chapters.title: Challenges to and Restoration of the Congress System
chapters.summary: 1967, splits, 1971, populism. From dominance to competition.

chapters.title: The Crisis of Democratic Order
chapters.summary: JP movement, Emergency 1975–77, 42nd Amendment, lessons for constitutionalism. Handle factually.

chapters.title: Rise of Popular Movements
chapters.summary: Chipko, Dalit Panthers, farmers, women, NBA. Movements as extra-parliamentary democracy.

chapters.title: Regional Aspirations
chapters.summary: Punjab, North-East, Jammu & Kashmir, Dravidian politics, Jharkhand–Chhattisgarh–Uttarakhand. Accommodation vs insurgency.

chapters.title: Recent Developments in Indian Politics
chapters.summary: Mandal, mandir, coalition era, 2014 majority politics, GST and federal bargaining as CA overlay. Keep analytical, not partisan.

chapters.title: Cold War and NAM (world politics)
chapters.summary: Bipolarity, NAM’s space, UN, arms race. Useful for IR theory in GS-II.

chapters.title: US Hegemony & Alternative centres
chapters.summary: Post-1991, EU, ASEAN, China, BRICS, multipolar talk. Read with current QUAD/BRICS news.

chapters.title: UN and Security in the Contemporary World
chapters.summary: UN organs, reform debate, new security (terrorism, human security, environment).
